coach_says: TSB is critically low at -55.5 and Garmin status is UNPRODUCTIVE, which triggers the hard constraint: one quality session maximum this week, everything else easy or rest. The Tuesday evening MTB group ride is that quality session and is non-negotiable; all other sessions are kept easy, short, or restorative to allow fatigue to clear. Aerobic-high shortage is noted but cannot be addressed safely this week — that priority carries forward to next week once TSB recovers.

days.details: Full-body mobility and light yoga flow. Focus on hip flexors, thoracic spine, hamstrings and glutes. No loading. Treat as active recovery only.

Non-negotiable committed group ride. Ride to effort with the group — no additional structure required. This is the single quality session for the week. If a morning road ride also occurs, keep it Zone 1-2 only and cap at 45 min to limit cumulative damage on an already fatigued system.
Mandatory recovery day post-Tuesday. No cycling, no gym, no structured activity. Sleep, nutrition, and hydration are the priority. Light walking around the house is fine but no deliberate exercise.

45 min | Objective: Active Recovery / Aerobic Flush
10 min Zone 1 easy warm-up
25 min Zone 1-2 steady (RPE 2-3, conversational, HR well below threshold)
10 min Zone 1 cool-down
No surges, no efforts. If legs feel dead, shorten to 30 min or swap for a walk.

90 min | Objective: Low-stress aerobic volume / TSB restoration
15 min Zone 1 warm-up
60 min Zone 2 steady (RPE 3-4, fully conversational, no drifting into Zone 3)
15 min Zone 1 cool-down
Keep cadence comfortable. This is not a tempo ride — discipline on intensity is critical this week. If TSB is still very negative or fatigue remains high, shorten to 60 min.

60 min easy walk or light hike. Flat to moderate terrain only — no hard climbing. Focus on mental recovery and time outdoors. This supports parasympathetic recovery without adding meaningful training stress.
Full rest day or optional 20-30 min gentle yoga / stretching if motivation is present. No structured training. Use the day to consolidate the week's recovery before next week's load begins.
